finding_types.label: SQL Injection
finding_types.description: Input changes executable SQL structure instead of remaining a data value, potentially changing what the database reads or writes.
finding_types.interpretation: An SQL Injection pill identifies the risk family being reviewed. String-built executable SQL is poor practice to remediate even without a proven exploit; a library-managed search value may remain unresolved. The finding status and evidence determine the actual claim. The pill alone does not confirm injection.
finding_types.remediation: Use the verified driver's parameter-binding API for values. Review dynamic identifiers separately. Keep business-field validation independent of query-structure protection.

finding_types.label: NoSQL Injection
finding_types.description: Untrusted input changes a NoSQL query's operators, selector structure, or executable expression rather than remaining an allowed data value.
finding_types.interpretation: Executable $where string construction is poor practice to refactor even without a proven exploit. An unmodeled document constraint alone is Review, not an established defect. Inspect actual value types, keys, transformations, library behavior, and the named status.
finding_types.remediation: Prefer data-only query APIs, constrain scalar slots and permitted keys/operators, and avoid building executable $where strings from input.

finding_types.label: Input Validation
finding_types.description: Server-side checks enforce the business requirements for a field, such as required presence, runtime type, permitted format, range, or length.
finding_types.interpretation: Poor input validation means an applicable requirement is not adequately enforced. This neutral family label also covers unresolved checks and supported protection: no validator identified in an analyzed slice is not proof that every execution path lacks validation. Free-text punctuation is not itself a defect.
finding_types.remediation: Define field-specific requirements and enforce them before use on all applicable paths. Verify guard behavior and middleware. Apply destination-specific protection separately.

finding_types.label: Account Creation Validation
finding_types.description: Required account fields and enforcing guards must be checked before an account is persisted.
finding_types.interpretation: Review field requirements, conditional bypasses, and generated persistence behavior. A modeled create operation alone does not prove a registration bypass.
finding_types.remediation: Enforce required fields before persistence, terminate rejected paths, add appropriate database constraints, and test the persisted result.

finding_types.label: Outbound Request Safety
finding_types.description: Input used in an outbound request may affect its destination, headers, or other request values. Unrestricted destination control can lead to server-side request forgery (SSRF).
finding_types.interpretation: The current scanner records bounded outbound-use evidence. A pill does not establish SSRF, destination reachability, or complete response-flow analysis.
finding_types.remediation: Verify allowed destinations and protocols, redirect handling, network boundaries, and sensitive request values for the specific HTTP client.

finding_types.label: Reflected XSS
finding_types.description: Request-controlled content is reflected into a browser response in a context that allows it to execute as script.
finding_types.interpretation: XSS means cross-site scripting. This glossary entry is vocabulary for a planned detector; the current reporting increment does not detect or assign Reflected XSS findings.
finding_types.remediation: Use context-appropriate output encoding and safe template or DOM APIs. Input validation alone does not replace correct output handling.

finding_types.label: Sensitive Data Logging
finding_types.description: Logs expose credentials, tokens, personal information, or other sensitive values to readers or storage that should not receive them.
finding_types.interpretation: Covers verified console and winston calls in analyzed route handlers that receive request values with credential or personal-data evidence. A field name is a hint for review, not proof; Authorization and Cookie headers are credentials by HTTP semantics. Morgan request logging that records URLs is checked against credentials read from the query string. Constant messages are not leaks. Non-request secrets and logger redaction configuration are not yet analyzed.
finding_types.remediation: Avoid logging secrets; minimize sensitive fields and apply verified redaction before emission. Review log access and retention.

finding_types.label: Sensitive Operation Review
finding_types.description: A possible sensitive use was recorded but does not yet map to a more specific supported risk family.
finding_types.interpretation: This is an analysis category. Inspect the evidence and missing operation semantics before making a security claim.
finding_types.remediation: Resolve the source, operation, API behavior, and required protection before selecting a fix.

findings.title: Possible sensitive data in a log entry
findings.summary: A verified logging call receives a request value whose field name or container suggests credentials or personal data, or that passes through an unresolved transformation. Confirm what the value contains and whether redaction applies before changing behavior. A field name is a hint, not proof.
findings.input_validation: Field validation is reported separately; it does not change what this log line contains.
findings.use_protection: Logging evidence: request body field password has a credential field-name hint and its content is written to the log.
findings.uncertainty: Review the evidence for the named claim. Independent findings review and runtime confirmation have not been performed. Semantic assessment was not run.

recommendations.title: Keep credential and personal-data content out of logs
actions: Remediate established vulnerabilities and poor practice. For Review items, resolve the named evidence before deciding whether or how behavior needs to change.
Remove the value from the log entry, or log a non-revealing fact (presence, length, match result, or a non-reversible identifier) instead.
Log an allowlist of fields rather than whole request bodies, queries, or header sets. Never log Authorization or Cookie header values.
If redaction is required, apply a verified redaction before the logger call or in the logger's configuration, and test that emitted lines no longer contain the value.
Do not send credentials in URL query strings; access logs, proxies, and browser history record URLs. Use a request body or header instead.

// Illustrative: log a fact about the credential, not the credential.
console.info('login attempt', { username, passwordProvided: typeof password === 'string' && password.length > 0 });

Intentionally Vulnerable TypeScript Application

This application contains numerous security vulnerabilities for testing purposes.

Available Endpoints:

  • POST /api/login - SQL Injection
  • GET /api/ping?host=example.com - Command Injection
  • GET /api/files?filename=test.txt - Path Traversal
  • GET /api/search?query=test - XSS
  • GET /api/proxy?url=http://example.com - SSRF
  • POST /api/calculate - RCE via eval
  • DELETE /api/admin/users/1 - Missing Authentication
  • GET /api/users/1 - IDOR
  • POST /api/parse-xml - XXE Injection
  • POST /api/parse-yaml - YAML Deserialization
  • POST /api/register - Mass Assignment
  • GET /api/debug - Sensitive Data Exposure
  • POST /api/validate-email - ReDoS
  • GET /api/token - Insecure Randomness
  • GET /redirect?url= - Open Redirect
  • POST /api/merge - Prototype Pollution
`); }
